<tools>
- codemode: Run JavaScript that calls other tools
- make_tool: Define a tested, versioned tool the agent can call later from eval_js
- eval_js: Run JS in this session. Find kept tools with tool_query, then await tools.NAME(args). Do not expect kept tools in the Pi tool list.
- tool_query: Search kept selftools by the job to do (Pi's own tools: use tool_search)
- tool_read: Read a kept tool's schema after tool_query
- web_search: Web research. Prefer {queries:[...]} with 2-4 varied angles; omit provider unless overriding the default.
- source_check: Gather source evidence with passage citations for a claim.
- fetch_content: Use to fetch URL content, direct images, GitHub repos, and videos.
- get_search_content: Use after web_search, source_check, or fetch_content to read stored content; findText finds passages without paging.
- unfold: unfold(codes) — restore context folded by Accordion (blocks tagged {#<code> FOLDED}).
- recall: recall(codes, query?) — read folded content or search within it right now without changing your standing context.
- run_tests: Run tests with compact output (auto-detects framework). Use instead of bash for test commands.
- subagent: Choose joined for prerequisites, detached only for optional results, and subagent_followup for related successful work. Batch independent assignments with a real parallel tool batch. Children have isolated conversations but share your filesystem; provide self-contained tasks and avoid overlapping ownership.

Additional tools may be available.
</tools>

<rules>
- Use codemode to batch independent tool calls (Promise.allSettled), chain them, or filter large output, instead of many separate calls.
- Before creating a tool, search kept tools with tool_query for the job and broader workflow, and check Pi tools with tool_search. A search miss is not proof that no related tool exists.
- When fixing or extending an existing workflow, inspect its current tool with tool_read and obtain its implementation and tests. Extend the owner rather than creating a renamed copy, _v2, or competing tool. For kept tools, call make_tool with the same name and preserve existing behavior, safety guards, and tests unless the user requests a change.
- If a Pi tool owns the workflow, use its supported configuration or modify its owning source when available and within scope. Do not shadow it with a new kept tool.
- If the user refers to a previous tool you cannot locate, its implementation cannot be safely extended, or a new tool would overlap with it and the choice is unclear, explain what you found and ask the user how to proceed instead of silently creating another tool.
- Create a new tool proactively only for a clearly distinct reusable job with no existing owner, using make_tool with name, description, JSON Schema, JS/TS code, and a test. Use normal tools for one-off jobs.
- make_tool keeps the tool only if at least one non-skipped child-process test passes. Failed or all-skipped tests are discarded.
- Write a description that says the job the tool does. Later turns search by that job with tool_query, read the schema with tool_read, and call it from eval_js as await tools.NAME(args). Set expose: true only for a small set of frequently used tools, and for workflows that call Pi tools from other extensions (so nested ctx.executeTool works).
- To compose existing tools, pass depends_on (e.g. ['web_search','fetch_content','web_enable'] from pi-web-access) and call them as await tools.NAME(args). Do not rebuild web_search. Tests must fakeTools({ web_search, fetch_content, web_enable }). pi-web-access tools stay disabled until web_enable; a workflow should call it once and retry if nested search/fetch report not-found.
- For live/network checks use t.skip() or test.skip(), or set requires_env / network so missing creds skip instead of passing. Declare test_env names to opt into copying those variables into the isolated test process; values are never logged.
- Use list_generations, rollback_tools, forget_tool, and /selftools to inspect, restore, or drop kept tools.
- tool_query searches only kept tools, by the job you want to do (e.g. 'count words in a text'), not a tool name. Never rebuild web_search or fetch_content from pi-web-access; workflows compose them with depends_on.
- Call a kept tool from eval_js as await tools.NAME(args). tools.query and tools.describe inside eval_js are aliases of tool_query / tool_read.
- Kept tools are not separate Pi tools unless they were created with expose: true.
- eval_js is live for this session only. Promote reusable code with make_tool.
- Call tool_query with the task ('count words in a text'), not a guessed tool name. It searches only kept selftools.
- For Pi's own tools (other extensions, MCP servers, deferred tools such as pi-web-access web_search), use Pi's built-in tool_search, not tool_query.
- Never rebuild web_search or fetch_content; to chain them, make_tool a workflow with depends_on: ['web_search','fetch_content','web_enable'] and expose: true.
- Kept tools: tool_read then eval_js with await tools.NAME(args), or call directly if exposed.
- When you see a `{#<code> FOLDED}` marker in your context (e.g. `{#3f9a2c FOLDED}`), that block was compacted by Accordion to save tokens — the full content is preserved, not lost. If the summary is not enough for your current task, call `unfold` with the code(s) from the marker(s) to restore them; the content returns on your next turn.
- When you see a `{#<code> FOLDED}` marker and need the full content for the current step, call `recall` with the code(s). Use recall's optional query when you need only matching fragments from the specified block(s); omit query when you need the full original content. Prefer `recall` over `unfold` when you only need the detail once; use `unfold` when you want the block to stay open across future turns.
- When running tests, use run_tests instead of bash. run_tests returns compact output that saves context tokens.
- Do NOT use bash to run test commands (npm test, vitest, jest, dotnet test, go test, pytest). Use run_tests instead.
- If run_tests returns a fallback message suggesting bash, THEN use bash with the exact command it provides.
- When the test project root (containing jest.config.js, package.json, or vitest.config.ts) is a subdirectory, pass cwd. Example: run_tests({ command: 'npx jest', cwd: 'C:/GitRepos/MyProject/Web' })
- If no framework is found, use the nested project candidates and exact cwd retry commands in the result instead of guessing a repository root.
- Stay in your own loop by default: your context connects each step's results, while a child hands back a lossy summary. Use subagent only when one of these applies.
- FLOOD: the work needs material you won't reuse that would flood your context — a survey across many areas of a repo, huge logs or outputs -> explore/shell child that returns only conclusions.
- PARALLEL: independent research paths that need nothing from each other or from this conversation -> one child each, launched in the same tool batch (or codemode Promise.all), each returning the same compact report shape.
- VERIFY: after a non-trivial change with a checkable requirement -> fresh explore child checks it as a black box; give it the goal and the diff, not your conclusions.
- Stay in the loop for: continuing an investigation or debugging trace you already started, updating a plan or doc, explaining your own work, clarifying or judging options from this conversation, resolving conflicts, coupled edits, small edits, and single lookups. One causal chain is never split across children.
- If you delegate, do it before reading that material yourself. Children research and verify; you keep the design calls and every edit.
- Children see none of this conversation and have no MCP/extension tools: give the goal, known facts and paths, constraints, and the report you want. explore cannot run commands; use shell when the child needs git, builds, or tests.
- Treat child reports as leads: check the claims you rely on against the code before acting on them or writing them into an answer, plan, or document.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

<project_instructions path="F:\MyWork\pi-selftools\AGENTS.md">
# AGENTS.md

This repo is **pi-selftools**: a Pi extension that ports NodeCode's "keep what the agent defines" idea to Node/TypeScript. The agent writes a tool, proves it with a test, and keeps it in a git-versioned folder (`~/.pi/agent/selftools`, override with `PI_SELFTOOLS_DIR`). Each commit there is a **generation**. Deeper docs: `README.md` (full reference) and `docs/compare-nodecode.md` (NodeCode mapping).

Two jobs can bring you here. Read the part that fits:

- **Part 1:** use the selftools tools proactively while doing any task. Don't wait for the user to name them.
- **Part 2:** change this extension's own code.

---

## Part 1: Using the tools (do this without being asked)

If `tool_query`, `tool_read`, `eval_js`, and `make_tool` are missing from your tool list, the extension isn't loaded. Tell the user to run `pi install .` (from this repo) or start with `pi -e .`. Don't fake them with bash.

The only key is `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` (optional; it improves `tool_query` ranking). It lives in `.env` at the repo root, with `.env.example` as the template, and pi-selftools loads it into the Pi process at startup. Without it, `tool_query` only matches keywords. Never print, log, or commit its value.

### Decision flow

For any capability you might need (search the web, convert a file, call a service), take these steps **before** writing a one-off script or saying you can't:

1. **`tool_query({ query: "<the job, in plain words>" })`.** Phrase it as the task ("count words in a text"), not a guessed tool name. It searches **only kept tools** (made with `make_tool`). Pi's own tools (other extensions, MCP servers, deferred tools like pi-web-access's `web_search`) are found with Pi's built-in **`tool_search`**, or are already in your tool list.
2. Act on the result:
   - Hit: run `tool_read({ name })` for the schema, then call it inside `eval_js` with `return await tools.NAME(args)`. If it only partially covers the request, follow **Extend existing tools before creating new ones** below. Kept tools are **not** in your Pi tool list unless they were made with `expose: true`.
   - `missing: true`: first check whether a Pi tool already does the job (`tool_search`) and search kept tools for the broader workflow, not just the new feature. A search miss is not proof that no related tool exists. Web search and page fetching are pi-web-access's `web_search` / `fetch_content`: **call those, never rebuild them.** If the job is a one-off, just do it with normal tools. If it's **reusable** (likely to come up again in this or a future session), apply the reuse checks below before building it with `make_tool`. `/selftools misses` lists past misses worth investigating, not automatic permission to create tools.
3. **Chain steps in one `eval_js`** instead of making one model round trip per step. Globals persist for the session (`n = 1` is still there next call). Helpers: `tools.query`, `tools.describe`, `tools.list()`, `tools.NAME(args)`, `callTool(name, args)`, `sh(cmd)`, `readFile`, `writeFile`, `console.log`.

### Extend existing tools before creating new ones

- **An adjustment is not a new tool by default.** When the user asks to fix, refine, or add a feature to an existing workflow, find and extend its current tool. Preserve its name, existing behavior, safety guards, and tests unless the user requests a change. For kept tools, use `make_tool` with the **same name**; do not create a renamed copy, `_v2`, or a competing tool for the same job.
- **Check ownership before creating.** Inspect related kept tools with `tool_read` and available Pi tool descriptions. Prefer an existing tool that owns the workflow even if it lacks the exact requested feature today. If a Pi tool owns it, use its supported configuration or modify its owning source when available and within the task's scope; do not shadow it with a new kept tool.
- **Ask when the choice is unclear.** If the user refers to a previous tool you cannot locate, you cannot safely extend its implementation, or a separate tool would overlap with it, explain what you found and ask whether to extend the existing tool or create a separate one. Do not silently choose a new tool. A clearly distinct reusable job with no existing owner may still be created proactively.
- **Example:** if a GitHub PR-review tool already lists pending reviews, requests to add filters, PBI details, history, or changed-since-last-check reporting belong in that tool—not in a second GitHub-review tool. If you cannot access the original implementation, ask the user how to proceed.

### Mandatory secret-safety rules for every tool

Apply these rules when creating, replacing, testing, or calling any tool, including helpers and workflows. Secret values must stay outside the agent's context.

- **Use `.env` for keys.** Prefer a user-managed, git-ignored `.env` loaded into the runtime environment. Tool code should access only the specific environment variable names it needs; never hardcode credentials or accept secret values as tool arguments. This repo's `.env` and `.env.example` remain limited to `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`; ask before adding other keys here. For other tools, document required variable names and use placeholders only in examples.
- **Do not read secrets into the conversation.** Never use file readers, shell commands, `eval_js`, searches, or other tools to inspect `.env`, private keys, credential stores, or secret-bearing configuration. Do not dump the environment. Do not ask the user to paste secrets into chat. If a key is missing, name the variable and ask the user to configure it locally; report only configured/missing, never its value.
- **Runtime use is not agent access.** A tool may consume a named credential internally to authenticate to its intended service, but must never return it to the agent or pass it to another model. Keep credentials out of generated source, tests, tool metadata, receipts, logs, stdout/stderr, errors, artifacts, and git history. Encoded, partial, or otherwise transformed secrets are not safe output either.
- **Build a safety net into the tool.** Return only explicitly allowed result fields. Handle errors with safe messages instead of raw request/response dumps, headers, URLs containing credentials, or stack traces that may expose secrets. Redact sensitive data before any logging or output; do not rely solely on the extension's error scrubbing. Send credentials only to the intended, trusted service, not caller-controlled destinations or redirects.
- **Refuse secret-reading capabilities.** Do not create a tool that reveals credentials, dumps environment variables, or bypasses these rules. Tools that read/search files or run commands must restrict access to the minimum needed. File-access guards must reject secret files and out-of-scope paths, including traversal and symlink escapes; fail closed when safety cannot be established. Do not provide an unrestricted command path as a workaround.
- **Prove the safety net with tests.** Use fake credentials and mocked services, never real keys. Verify that success results, errors, and captured logs do not contain the fake secret or its transformations; test missing-key handling and applicable forbidden-path/destination rejection. Pass environment opt-ins by name with `test_env`, never by value, and only when needed.

These are mandatory agent instructions, **not a sandbox or an enforced permission boundary**. Kept tools still run with Pi's full permissions. If a tool cannot meet these rules, do not create or run it; explain the limitation without inspecting secrets.

### make_tool checklist

- `name`: `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$`. Not reserved (core tool names, `read`, `bash`, `edit`, `write`, `grep`, `find`, `ls`, `search`, `query`, `describe`, `list`, `powershell`) and not a Windows device name (`con`, `nul`, `com1`, ...).
- `description`: state the **job** it does. `tool_query` searches on it later, so a vague description means the tool never gets found.
- `parameters`: JSON Schema with `type: "object"`.
- `code`: `export async function execute(params, tools) { ... }`, a default export, or just the body. Follow the mandatory secret-safety rules above and include the applicable guards and safety tests.
- `test`: needs at least **one non-skipped passing** `node:test` test, or nothing is kept. In scope: `execute`, `assert`, `test`, `skipIfNoEnv(t)`, `fakeTools({...})`. The test child gets a minimal env (PATH, HOME/temp, `NODE_*`). Opt secrets in by **name** with `test_env`. For live or network checks, use `t.skip()` or `requires_env` so a check that never ran shows as a skip, not a pass.
- Workflows that call other tools: list every name in `depends_on`, fake every one in the test, and set `expose: true` if any dependency is a Pi tool. Nested Pi calls only work through `ctx.executeTool`, which `eval_js` doesn't have. For pi-web-access, include `web_enable` (its tools stay disabled until enabled). See `src/examples/topic-digest.ts`.
- `expose: true` only for a few frequently used tools, plus workflows that call Pi tools. Keep the Pi tool list small.

### When a kept tool misbehaves

- **Fix a kept tool by calling `make_tool` again with the same name.** The extension commits to the tools repo for you: `keep NAME`, `replace NAME`, `forget NAME`, `rollback to N`. **Never edit or `git commit` inside `~/.pi/agent/selftools` by hand.** That skips the test gate and confuses the generation history.
- Replacing an existing name puts the new version in a **held** state. It's live right away, gets committed on its first successful real call, and reverts automatically if that first call throws. Check the receipt and don't loop on rebuilds.
- `list_generations` then `rollback_tools({ generation })` restores an earlier set (as a new commit; history is kept). `forget_tool({ name })` drops one tool and warns about dependent workflows.
- `eval_js` code is **not** saved anywhere. Promote anything reusable with `make_tool`.
- Nothing here is sandboxed. Kept tools run with Pi's full permissions and env.

---

## Part 2: Working on this repo

### Commands

```bash
npm test            # node --test test/*.test.ts (~40s; spawns child node processes and temp git repos)
npm run typecheck   # tsc --noEmit
npm run eval:instructions -- --allow-network  # opt-in model-backed behavioral evals
node --test test/search.test.ts   # one file
pi -e .             # try the extension in Pi without installing
```

Requires Node >= 22.19 and `git` on PATH. There's no build step: Node runs the `.ts` files directly with type stripping. Use **erasable TypeScript only** (no `enum`, `namespace`, or constructor parameter properties), and import with explicit `.ts` extensions (`import { x } from "./paths.ts"`).

### Instruction changes require evals

- Whenever adding or changing agent instructions (`AGENTS.md`, runtime `promptGuidelines`, tool descriptions, or decision hints), add or update behavioral cases in `evals/` for the intended decision and a plausible regression. Do not treat a text-match assertion as proof that the agent follows an instruction.
- Default eval model: **`openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol`**, thinking **`high`**. Keep this default in `evals/config.mjs`; overrides must be explicit. Never silently switch models when the requested model or login is unavailable.
- Run the offline harness tests with `npm test` and, for instruction changes, run `npm run eval:instructions -- --allow-network` using Pi's configured local login. Report model, thinking level, and outcomes. If inference cannot run, report it as unverified/blocked—not passed—and ask the user to configure access locally; never request secrets in chat.
- Keep tool actions mocked, model-generated code/tests inert, and real credentials outside prompts, traces, logs, and artifacts. Cover both forbidden actions and legitimate tool creation so the eval does not reward simply refusing every request. See `evals/README.md` for the harness contract and limitations.

### Committing changes

After you fix or change code in **this repo**, commit it yourself. Don't leave changes uncommitted.

1. Run `npm test` and `npm run typecheck`. Both must pass. If a test was already failing, say so and don't commit over it silently.
2. One logical change per commit: a bug fix and a docs update are two commits.
3. Message style matches the history: an imperative subject of 72 characters or less ("Fix test-gate count parsing on Node 26"), a blank line, then a short body explaining **why**.
4. Never commit `node_modules/`, `.pi/`, `tmp/`, `.env`, or secrets. `.env.example` holds only `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`. Don't add other keys without asking the user. **Don't push, amend, or rewrite history without asking the user.**

### Layout

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `src/extension.ts` | Pi entry: registers the 7 tools and `/selftools*` commands. `promptGuidelines` here is what Pi shows the model at runtime |
| `src/instructions.ts` | Shared tool-ownership runtime guidance and miss hint, exercised by instruction evals |
| `evals/` | Opt-in model rollouts with fake tools and deterministic trace grading |
| `src/selftools.ts` | `Selftools` class: git-backed tools dir, keep/replace/held/forget/rollback, `misses.jsonl` |
| `src/runner.ts`, `src/wrap.ts`, `src/env.ts` | Test gate: wraps code and test, runs `node --test --test-reporter=tap` in a child with a minimal env, parses counts (`src/schema.ts`) |
| `src/search.ts`, `src/jev.ts` | `tool_query`/`tool_read`: lexical recall plus an optional Jev judge (`TYPESAFE_API_KEY`). Never throws; falls back to lexical |
| `src/eval-js.ts` | Session `vm` context behind `eval_js` |
| `src/call.ts` | Bridge for nested calls: kept tool, then Pi `ctx.executeTool`, then test fake |
| `src/examples/` | `topic_digest`: worked workflow over pi-web-access `web_search` + `fetch_content` |
| `test/helpers.ts` | `withSelftools()` (a fresh temp tools repo per test) and the `WORD_COUNT` fixture |

### Conventions

- Tests use `node:test` + `node:assert/strict`. Always go through `withSelftools()`. **Never touch the real `~/.pi/agent/selftools`.** Mock `fetch` and use `fakeTools`. No live network calls in tests.
- Never log secret values. Receipts redact `test_env` values, and errors scrub `Bearer ...` tokens and env values. Keep it that way.
- Tool results: `{ content: [{ type: "text", text }], details, isError? }`. Set `isError: true` on rejections and misses so the Pi UI shows a failure.
- When you change the tool surface (names, params, behavior), update all of these together: the `promptGuidelines` and descriptions in `src/extension.ts`, Part 1 of this file, `README.md`, and, if it affects NodeCode parity, `docs/compare-nodecode.md`.
- Only use Pi's public extension API (`registerTool`, `registerCommand`, `on`, `getAllTools`). Types for it live in `src/pi-coding-agent.d.ts`.

</project_instructions>

Ask the durable supervisor to terminate a running job and its process tree. Final status is confirmed by the supervisor, not guessed from a persisted PID.

Codemode: `tools.bg_kill(args)` resolves to a string.

toolsAdded.name: bg_input
toolsAdded.description:
Queue stdin input for the durable supervisor, including after reopening the parent session.

Codemode: `tools.bg_input(args)` resolves to a string.

toolsAdded.name: run_tests
toolsAdded.description:
Run project tests and return compact pass/fail output. Use this INSTEAD of bash for all test execution. Auto-detects vitest, jest, dotnet, go, pytest.

Codemode: `tools.run_tests(args)` resolves to a string.

command.description: Override the auto-detected test command. E.g. 'dotnet test tests/Api.Tests'

lines.description: Number of tail lines to show on failure (default 40)

cwd.description: Working directory to run tests from. Defaults to process.cwd(). Pass this when the test project root (jest.config.js, package.json) lives in a subdirectory.

toolsAdded.name: subagent
toolsAdded.description:
Run an isolated in-process Pi subagent. JOINED by default: required reports return after cleanup. Detached mode is only for optional results delivered later. Use subagent_followup for related successful work with saved conversation/configuration. Batch independent calls with a real parallel tool batch; never batch dependent edits with prerequisite research. Isolated context, shared filesystem. Capacity 6 across both modes; overflow fails explicitly. Types: explore (read-only), shell (commands/logs).

Codemode: `tools.subagent(args)` resolves to a string.

type.description: Subagent type. explore=read-only investigation, shell=command-oriented investigation.

task.description: Task to delegate to the subagent.

cwd.description: Working directory for the subagent. Defaults to the current cwd.

model.description: Optional model override. Use provider/model or a model id in the active provider, optionally followed by :level (for example provider/model:high).

timeoutSeconds.description: Optional timeout in seconds. Packet calls honor up to 300 seconds; ordinary calls use a 600-second minimum; calls without a timeout default to 1800 seconds.

evidencePacket.description: Optional selected EvidencePacketV1 slice. Invalid packets visibly fall back to prose.

mode.description: Defaults to joined: required result returned after child cleanup. Detached is only for optional results delivered later.

background.description: Legacy alias: true=detached, false=joined. Must agree with mode; omission defaults to joined.

toolsAdded.name: subagent_resume
toolsAdded.description:
Only when the user requests recovery: recover an interrupted subagent into a NEW background run using its saved task and checkpoint. Inspect possible side effects first. This is a checkpoint handoff, not exact execution replay; never automatically rerun interrupted shell actions.

Codemode: `tools.subagent_resume(args)` resolves to a string.

toolsAdded.name: subagent_followup
toolsAdded.description:
Explicit related follow-up for a successful normal child. Reuses its saved model/tools/prompt and disk transcript exclusively, never interrupted work. Joined by default; bounded fresh handoff after 3 assignments, 1 MiB, or unsafe context. No implicit reuse.

Codemode: `tools.subagent_followup(args)` resolves to a string.

jobId.description: Successful normal child to reuse explicitly: the latest returned job ID, not an ancestor; never an interrupted or packet child.

toolsAdded.name: subagent_wait
toolsAdded.description:
Retrieve joined or detached child reports. waitFor=all (default) waits for every target; any returns after at least one terminal outcome. No IDs includes running and undelivered finished jobs. Timeout defaults to 120s, max 240s; timeout/abort stops waiting, never children. Detached results also deliver later; joined results do not.

Codemode: `tools.subagent_wait(args)` resolves to a string.

waitFor.description: Defaults to all. Any returns after at least one targeted terminal outcome.

jobIds.description: Child job ids (e.g. 'sa-1'). Defaults to running and undelivered finished jobs.

timeoutSeconds.description: Maximum seconds to wait. Default 120, max 240.

toolsAdded.name: subagent_status
toolsAdded.description:
Snapshot of durable joined/detached children, context usage (unknown when unavailable), transcripts and reuse metadata. Do not poll; call only for requested progress or explicit recovery discovery. Joined outcomes are retrieved by their launch receipt or subagent_wait, never automatically redelivered.

Codemode: `tools.subagent_status(args)` resolves to a string.

jobId.description: Child job id. Omit for all jobs.

toolsAdded.name: subagent_cancel
toolsAdded.description:
Cancel a running child. Joined cancellation awaits cleanup and returns its terminal report; detached cancellation requests delivery of the partial outcome later.

Codemode: `tools.subagent_cancel(args)` resolves to a string.

That file is the herdr-app resume bridge:

`C:\Users\Admin\.config\herdr-app\session-bridge\session-bridge.ps1`

Dot-sourced (`. "...ps1"`) from `$PROFILE` it only wraps `codex/copilot/cursor-agent` when `HC_TERMINAL_ID` is set and `HERDR_PANE_ID` is not. Outside herdr-core it's a no-op.

Current state here:
- bridge: present
- `hc.exe`: present
- `HC_TERMINAL_ID`: set / `HERDR_PANE_ID`: unset
- Pi stub `~/.pi/agent/extensions/hc-session-label.ts`: missing — so Pi sessions aren't recorded

Running that dot-source line in my transient shell wouldn't persist — wrappers die with the process. To wire it persistently (profile + Claude hook + Pi/OpenCode stubs) is:

`pwsh -NoProfile -File "C:\Users\Admin\.config\herdr-app\session-bridge\session-bridge.ps1" -Install`
